institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I found both the city and the university interesting, and both things lived up the expectations :)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy of various reasons 1) a lot of information was in french, 2) it was difficult knowing who to contact for help, both at UCPH and SciencesPo.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived I received a lot of help from SciencesPo and the process of getting into courses were more relaxed than in Denmark; it is okay to start a course and then change during the first weeks. There were also an introduction week where people were very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I don't think there is any campus housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
If you want to live in a student housing you can apply to Cité Universitaire, which is also more affordable and is about 20-30 minutes from SciencesPo. If you want to live in an apartment with others I can recommend the website
https://www.lacartedescolocs.fr/
. Apart from that there are also many websites and facebook groups that can help with finding housing. I think it's equally difficult to find a place to live in Copenhagen and Paris, but there are more small and affordable studio apartments in Paris, if you want to live alone :)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything went fine. I did have one problem: I took a language test that cost money, and found out later that I didn't have to do it anyway because I was from Denmark - even though it said so on SciencesPo and UCPH's website. So save your money :) !

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The administrative help of both UCPH and SciencesPo have been confusing, but there wasn't a lot of problems since I arrived at the university, as it was easier just to ask the administration in person, and then they are helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It wasn't difficult to get the courses I was interested in. There is a registration process before arriving that is confusing. But after I arrived I was admitted to most of my courses by asking the teacher if it's okay if you take the course and then beeing admitted by the administration. So don't worry if you don't get the courses you wanted on the day of course registration! Lots of people change courses within the first weeks.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though it seems stressful, don't worry, there are lots of interesting courses. The course registration website is confusing, and people sit ready with a list of courses they are interested in. So I can recommend doing the same and do some research before on what courses you are interested in, and then try to register for them as fast as possible when registration begins. But if you don't succeed (I didn't) it's often possible to enroll in them at a later time after your arrival.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were very interesting and of high quality

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was a bit higher than UCPH. The teachers have higher expectations to the students and the workload is higher regarding reading for the classes, class participation, exams and presentations. But the other students are also very engaged and passionate, which is inspiring :)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There are smaller classes, so each student have more time with the teacher. I resembles more the teaching style of gymnasium in Denmark. It is expected to a larger degree that the student participate a lot in class with presentations eg. 
And they also mark if you come to classes or not, and you fail the class if you consecutively don't show up to classes without a valid reason, which is something I had to get used to! They are however helpful/understanding if you get sick.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Sociology of Inequalities
 - Causal Analysis in Sociology 
 - Quantitative Methods I
 - Demography: Challenges and Policy Implications
 - Sociology of Migration
 - Francais Niveau A2

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sociology of Inequalities, Causal Analysis and french (or other language) classes if you can get it transferred :)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't visit other french cities as train tickets were more expensive than i thought. So if you want to travel around during your breaks or weekends be sure to put some money aside, so it's possible :) !

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The Navigo card is 75 € which is cheap in the light that you can travel freely in all of Île de France.
Groceries are a bit cheaper than in Copenhagen and so was restaurants, bars, cafés, concerts, cinemas etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many social activities at SciencesPo and many students participate in them. There is a rich student life. There are however fewer parties and no 'fredagsbar'/alcohol on campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend coming to the welcome week where you can meet other exchange students and also to register for sports, art classes etc. to meet people outside of your classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are many things to see in Paris, it's a very big city! I spent many days/weekends walking in the different areas, visiting museums, parks, stores etc. My experience was that the semester went by very fast and there was still lots of things to see towards the end :)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
It was easy, there are small differences from Denmark, but all in all the culture is somewhat similar. The language barrier was the most difficult, many french people are not good in english, especially older people, so I can recommend practising some french before going on the exchange. 
Apart from that people are very open and sociable!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Participate in activities hosted by SciencesPo and register for eg a sports team or art/language classes. 
People were generally very nice and open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Language barriers was by far the most difficult.
The administrative process were more relaxed which could be an issue when being used to the Danish way of doing it; In Denmark you register for courses the semester before and there is no way of changing it while at SciencesPo it was unclear which courses were available until just before the semester started and people were changing classes a lot.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were very open and friendly :) The food is very good, the city is very beautiful and the weather is slightly better than in Denmark

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Register for the introduction week, remember to socialize even though there is a lot of work during the semester and take french classes

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't need to take an english test/certificate!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The classes were very interesting and i met a lot of nice people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I am not used to doing presentations in front of other students in English, so I found it challenging to do it. But it was required for me to do it multiple times through the semester, both in French and English, so I got gradually more comfortable with it, and today I am happy i did it :)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
